title: persistence contract
description: The app's persistence facts, read by the persistence-and-migrations checker (check-persistence.mjs).

mode.description: tables: SQLite tables and repositories (the default). document: one validated JSON document in current/backup slots. both: tables plus a document for small app state.

databaseFile.description: The database file name in expo-sqlite's default directory.

protectedTables.description: Tables no reset may delete, update or drop: entitlements (purchase state) and diagnostics such as error_log.

resetModules.description: Repo-relative files that implement user-facing resets (Delete all my data). Every reset is listed here (not in sqlAllowed): the checker proves each one keeps the protected tables and runs in one transaction.

sqlAllowed.description: Files that may own SQL besides the repositories: an adapter outside the data folder that holds SQL text and the driver, or an infrastructure module in the data folder that runs statements (a debug read of PRAGMA page_count). A reset never goes here: list it in resetModules, where its protected tables and its transaction are checked. src/services/error-log/sqlite-error-log-adapter.ts is always allowed.

legacyImports.description: Files that may import an older storage engine (AsyncStorage, another SQLite binding) to copy its data into the app database once, guarded by a done flag. Remove the file and the entry once the import has shipped long enough.

rootComponent.description: The file that renders the app root and calls useCheckpointOnBackground once (Expo Router: src/app/_layout.tsx).

keyValueStore.description: The one key-value library for small preferences.

fixturesTest.description: The test that lists every frozen database fixture (default test/sqlite/migration-fixtures.test.ts).

document.description: Only for mode document or both.

appId.description: The identity every stored document carries; a document with another appId decodes as damaged.

protectedSections.description: Document sections no reset may write and only a dated revocation may downgrade.
